questions.question: What is an element of $A\times B$?
options: A subset containing all elements of $A$ and $B$
An ordered pair $(a,b)$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$
An unordered pair whose entries may come from either set
A number obtained by multiplying elements of $A$ and $B$

questions.question: Why does order matter in the Cartesian product?
options: Because sets always have a first and last element
Because $(a,b)$ records a first component and a second component
Because multiplication of numbers is not commutative
Because subsets cannot be ordered

questions.question: For finite sets, how is $\operatorname{card}(A\times B)$ computed?
options: $\operatorname{card}(A)+\operatorname{card}(B)$
$2^{\operatorname{card}(A)}$
$\operatorname{card}(A)\operatorname{card}(B)$
$\operatorname{card}(A)-\operatorname{card}(B)$

questions.question: Why is $A\times A$ used when defining a binary operation on $A$?
options: A binary operation takes one subset of $A$
A binary operation is a function from $A$ to $\mathbb{R}$ only
A binary operation always returns a pair outside $A$
A binary operation takes two inputs from $A$

questions.question: If $A=\{1,2\}$ and $B=\{x,y\}$, which pair belongs to $A\times B$?
If $A=\{0\}$ and $B=\{1,2,3\}$, what is $A\times B$?
options: $\varnothing$

questions.question: Why is $A\times B$ generally different from $B\times A$?
options: The allowed first and second coordinates are interchanged
The product ignores which set an entry comes from
The two products always have different cardinalities
Ordered pairs do not appear in either product

questions.question: In a binary operation $*\colon A\times A\to A$, what does closure mean?
options: Every input pair from $A\times A$ is assigned an output in $A$
The operation must be commutative for every pair of inputs
The operation has no output
Only one input from $A$ is allowed

questions.question: If $(p,q)\in A\times B$, which statement must be true?
options: $p\in B$ and $q\in A$
$p\in A$ and $q\in B$
$p=q$
$p$ and $q$ must both be subsets of $A$

questions.question: Why does the finite formula for $\operatorname{card}(A\times B)$ use multiplication rather than addition?
options: Each $a\in A$ pairs with $\operatorname{card}(B)$ second components
Only the largest of the two sets contributes pairs
Pairs are counted by subtracting repeated elements
Each element is counted only if it belongs to both sets

questions.question: When a product $A\times B$ is empty, what must be true?
options: $A$ and $B$ must have the same elements
Both $A$ and $B$ must be infinite
Both $A$ and $B$ must be nonempty
At least one of $A$ or $B$ is empty

questions.question: Let $A=\{0,1\}$. A binary operation on $A$ is a function from which domain to which codomain?
options: $A\times A$ to $A$
$A$ to $A\times A$
$2^A$ to $A\times A$
$A\cup A$ to $2^A$

questions.question: If $A$ is finite, nonempty, and $\operatorname{card}(A\times B)=0$, what can be concluded about $B$?
options: $B=A$
$B$ has one element
$B=\varnothing$
$B$ is countably infinite
